title: WT32-ETH01

onboard.what: Ethernet REF_CLK input from the 50 MHz oscillator
CFG pin, used for hardware factory reset

warnings.message: Use a supply that delivers at least 500 mA.

flash_hint: No USB port and no buttons: wire a 3.3 V USB-to-UART adapter to the PROG pins (adapter RX to TXD, adapter TX to RXD, GND to GND; keep the adapter at 3.3 V logic and power the board from a supply with at least 500 mA on 3V3 or on 5V, never both). Hold IO0 at GND while you pull EN low and release it, so the ESP32 starts the serial bootloader; flash, then free IO0 and reset again to run the firmware.
notes: Conflict: the schematic V1.4 names a net IO35_RXD2 next to EX_IO5. The datasheet V1.4 (table 2), the wiki and the schematic's own LED3 note (RXD2(IO5)) all say RXD = IO5 (RXD2), so IO-4 RXD is GPIO5 and IO-17 is GPIO35; the IO35_RXD2 net stays recorded as a conflict.

Header sides: read by eye from the manufacturer's photo (datasheet V1.4 p.7, back side) and drawn from the component side with the RJ45 at the bottom: left PROG 1-3 and IO 1-10, right PROG 4-6 and IO 11-20. Not machine-checkable.
Labels as printed in the datasheet tables, normalized: EN1 -> EN, 5V2 -> 5V, IO393 -> IO39, IO363 -> IO36 and 3V3 with note 2 on IO-7 (note digits), I014 -> IO14 (typo).
IO39, IO36 and IO35 are input only.
PROG (datasheet table 1) is the reserved debug and programming interface: TXD/RXD there are GPIO1/GPIO3 (TXD0/RXD0, UART0); TXD/RXD on IO-5/IO-4 are UART2 (GPIO17/GPIO5).
LINK (IO-10) is the PHY's network link LED line, not an ESP32 GPIO.
Ethernet (LAN8720A over RMII): MDC GPIO23, MDIO GPIO18, oscillator enable GPIO16, REF_CLK into GPIO0. GPIO0 is also a strapping pin: the oscillator must stay off while the ESP32 boots.
The pinned sources name no PSRAM for the WT32-S1 module; the module variant stays unknown, so the ESP32 rule for GPIO16/17 reports GPIO17 (IO-5 TXD) as caution.
The pinned sources state neither a USB port nor the antenna type; usb is empty and the module antenna unknown.
IO0 (PROG-6) goes to GND only for flashing (see flash_hint); in operation it carries the Ethernet REF_CLK and is not free for other uses.
